prompt_en: A high-detail Lunarpunk editorial night photograph of an unmistakably adult woman, her facial appearance and long wavy dark hair guided only by the supplied portrait, working as a lunar-tide ecologist at a floating wetland observatory. Beneath a huge visible crescent moon, she pours glowing blue-green algae culture from a handblown glass vessel into a crescent-shaped translucent bioreactor; the transfer visibly ignites pearlescent mycelium conduits woven through reeds and lily pools. She wears an indigo grown-fiber utility coat embroidered with lunar-phase arcs, seed capsules, and shell-fastened tools. Silver dew collectors, moon-phase gauges, moss-covered ceramic instruments, and living vine pipes make the station feel handcrafted yet advanced. The surrounding marsh is dark, misty, and thriving, lit by cool moonlight, bioluminescent fungi, and reflected violet-blue water. Photorealistic skin, tactile natural materials, credible working ecology, subtle grain, complex environmental storytelling. Use a medium-wide three-quarter environmental frame at wetland level: keep her face, hands, vessel, pouring stream, reactor, glowing conduits, wetland, and moon legible in one depth stack. A 35 mm documentary perspective makes the activation a diagonal cause-and-effect path across the water.
